headline: Grok Bot, the AI agent service from Elon Musk's SpaceX, now gets its own email address for signing up to services and contacting businesses.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: a clear product change quoted from the announcement, but the article gives no detail on limits or safeguards.
importance_line: What changed is that Grok Bot can now send and receive email as itself, which affects its users first, then the businesses it contacts, and the doubt is that the article is a how-to quoting the announcement and says nothing about safeguards or who is responsible for what it sends.
summary: 9to5Mac reports, quoting the announcement on X, that Grok Bot now has its own email address, ending in @mail.grokbot.com, which the agent can use to sign up for services, contact businesses and schedule time with someone for its user, and that users claim one by asking Bot or tagging @bot on X. It is the second upgrade this week, after an intelligence upgrade with help from Anthropic's Claude (our 8 Oct edition carried Musk's announcement that Grok Bot will choose among other firms' models), and 9to5Mac places it beside Meta's Muse and OpenAI's Dot agents.
notes: Url shortened (removed ?extended-comments=1). Owner named as SpaceX because our 8 Oct 2026 edition (Gizmodo) did; 9to5Mac's text does not name it. Our 9 Oct edition carried a Futurism report of Grok Bot posting a user's bank balances to a Slack channel.
